title: Causal Chain: From Training Data Poisoning to Rogue Agent Behavior — What Monitoring Can Detect This Late?

original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain: From Training Data Poisoning to Rogue Agent Behavior — What Monitoring Can Detect This Late?

**Problem:** Training data poisoning could cause a model to behave rogue under specific trigger conditions. By the time the rogue behavior appears, it may be too late — but monitoring might still be the last line of defense.

**Direction:** Take a small fine-tuned model with an embedded behavioral trigger (backdoor). Deploy it in an agent system with monitoring. Trigger the backdoor. Measure whether monitoring catches the resulting rogue behavior, and how quickly.

**Why it matters:** Training data poisoning bypasses pre-deployment evaluation. Monitoring is the only post-deployment defense. Characterizing monitoring effectiveness against backdoor-triggered rogue behavior is critical.

**Relevant context:** Training data poisoning (backdoor attacks); agent monitoring; last-line-of-defense monitoring.
